package_info.package_name: N/A (RepoJacking is a technique, not a specific package)
package_info.package_manager: Go, Swift, Packagist (and any GitHub-based package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of packages whose repositories were vulnerable to RepoJacking via username rename
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package becomes malicious when an attacker hijacks its repository namespace via RepoJacking, allowing them to serve arbitrary, potentially malicious code to all downstream users and dependencies.

execution_context.file_location: entire repository (attacker-controlled repo at hijacked namespace)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the hijacked package is imported or executed, the code accesses environment variables (e.g., SECRET_TOKEN) and exfiltrates their values to an attacker-controlled domain via HTTP POST, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server, which is a classic sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package code should not access secrets or send data to unknown external domains without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or error reporting libraries may send non-sensitive data to trusted domains, but not secrets.
key_indicators: Access to environment variables containing secrets
Network requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains
Code added after repository namespace takeover

execution_context.trigger: package installation or build (runtime or import-time)
execution_context.file_location: setup.php / main.go / main.swift (entrypoint of hijacked package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime or during installation, the code reads sensitive environment variables (e.g., DB_PASSWORD), writes them to a temporary file, and exfiltrates the data to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive credentials and sends them to an external server, which is not expected in legitimate package code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or exfiltrate user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or support tools may collect logs, but not secrets, and only with user consent.
key_indicators: Malicious code inserted after repository hijack

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers a previously used (now available) GitHub username matching a popular package's original owner.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to create a repository with the same namespace as the original package.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a repository with the same name as the original under the hijacked username.
attack_chain.leads_to: Hijacked namespace now points to attacker's repository.

attack_chain.action: Attacker adds malicious code to the hijacked repository (e.g., credential exfiltration, backdoors).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now distributed to all users who depend on the package.

attack_chain.action: Downstream users or CI/CD systems install or import the package, executing the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of secrets, compromise of developer or production environments.

behavioral_signatures: Sudden change in repository ownership or namespace for popular packages
Addition of code that accesses environment variables or secrets
Outbound network requests to untrusted or new domains from package code
Unexpected changes in package maintainer or repository URL
file_indicators: New or modified entrypoint files (main.go, setup.php, main.swift) after namespace change
Code accessing environment variables or writing to temporary files
References to external domains in code
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled or previously unseen domains
Unusual traffic from build or CI/CD environments to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes in package repository ownership or namespace, especially for popular packages. Flag packages whose codebase changes significantly after a namespace or maintainer change. Scan for code that accesses environment variables or makes outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Alert on installation or import of packages from recently hijacked namespaces, and monitor for exfiltration attempts from build or runtime environments.
